questions.question: National Income refers to ___________.

options.text: Money value of goods and services produced in a country during a year
Money value of stocks and shares of a country during a year
Money value of capital goods produced by a country during a year
Money value of consumer goods produced by a country during a year

questions.solution:
• National Income is defined as the total value of all the final goods and services produced by a country in a certain year.
 
• It includes all the payments made to all the resources in the forms of wages, interests, rent and profits.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers does not make an estuary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahanadi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Estuary**

 
 
• **An estuary is an area where a freshwater river or stream meets the ocean**. When freshwater and seawater combine, the water becomes brackish, or slightly salty.
 
• **Estuaries are home to unique plant and animal communities.**
 
• Estuaries are among the most productive ecosystems in the world. Many animals rely on estuaries for food, places to breed, and migration stopovers.
 
• **Congress created the National Estuarine Research Reserve System** to protect more than one million acres of estuarine land and water.
 
• Western flowing rivers widen their mouth into the sea, so these rivers form Estuaries whereas Eastern rivers flow through broken hills and mountain ranges
 
• The river that forms the estuary is Narmada, Tapi and Mandovi.
 
• **Mahanadi does not form an estuary as it forms a delta**.​​​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Mahanadi**

 
 
• The Mahanadi river originates at a height of 422 meters above mean sea level near Pharsiya village, Nagri town in the Raipur district of Chhattisgarh.
 
• Mahanadi river of peninsular India is one of the major interstate east-flowing rivers.
 
• The length of the Mahanadi river from its source of origin to its confluence in the Bay of Bengal is nearly 851km, of which 357 km lies in Chhattisgarh and the remaining 494 km in Odisha.
 
• In Water Potential the Mahanadi river ranks second to the Godavari river among the peninsular rivers.
 
 
 
• **Narmada**
 
 
• **Narmada is the longest river in Madhya Pradesh, followed by the Tapti.**
 
• Narmada is the largest west-flowing river in peninsular India.
 
• Its total length from its source in Amarkantak Amarkantak to its estuary in the Gulf of Khambhat is 1,310 km.
 
• The Source of the Narmada is Narmada Kund which is located at Amarkantak in Anuppur District, Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Narmada is also known as the Rewa.
 
 
 
• **​Tapi**​
 
 
• **The Tapti River (aka Tapi river )is a river in central India located to the south of the Narmada river which flows westwards before draining into the Arabian Sea**.
 
• The river has a length of around 724 km and flows through the states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Tapti river originates from Multai Betul district Madhya Pradesh. And also from the Satpura range.

questions.question: What is the number of groups and periods in the modern periodic table?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**18,7.**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• There are **18 groups__** and __**7 periods**__ in the modern periodic table.
 
• A period is a horizontal row of the periodic table. There are seven periods in the periodic table, with each one beginning at the far left.
 
• A group is a vertical column of the periodic table, based on the organization of the outer shell electrons. There are a total of 18 groups.

questions.question:
The plasma of the blood contains which among the following constituents?

I. Proteins

II. Salts

III. Hormones
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**All I, II and III**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• Plasma is the largest component of blood, comprising about 55% of its overall content.
 
• Along with water, plasma carries salts, hormones and enzymes.
 
• The main purpose of plasma is to transport nutrients, hormones, and proteins to the parts of the body that need them.
 
• Plasma is the largest part of the blood. It makes up more than half (about 55%) of its total content. When separated from the rest of the blood, plasma is a pale yellow liquid that contains water, salts, and enzymes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Plasma is called the matrix of blood. It is composed of clotting factors, protein compounds, and serum. 
 
• It consists of 92% water with proteins, salts, lipids, and glucose. 
 
• Plasma is the main mode of excretory product transport.
 
• The main role of plasma is to transport nutrients, hormones, and proteins to the parts of the body that need them. 
 
• Cells also dump their waste products into the plasma.
 
• The plasma then helps to remove this waste from the body. 
 
• Blood plasma also carries all parts of the blood through the body's circulatory system.
 
• Proteins and antibodies in plasma are also used in the treatment of rare chronic conditions such as autoimmune disorders and haemophilia.

questions.question: What is the basis of first level of classification among plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Differentiated plant body.**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The first level of classification among plants depends on whether the plant body has well- differentiated, distinct components.
 
• Depending upon these criteria plants are classified as Thallophyta, Bryophyta, and Pteridophyta.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Thallophyta

 
 
• The plant body is not differentiated from roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They are commonly called algae.
 
 
 
• Bryophyta
 
 
• These are small terrestrial plants.
 
• They show differentiation in the body design, with stem, leaf-like structures, and root-like structures.
 
 
 
• Pteridophyta
 
 
• The plant body is differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves, apart from having a specialized tissue for conduction.
 
 
 
• Gymnosperms
 
 
• Gymnosperms are plants with naked seeds.
 
 
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
• Angiosperms are seed-bearing plants. Seeds develop inside tissues that get modified to form the fruit of the plant.

questions.question: A body is initially moving with a velocity of 5 m/s. It undergoes an acceleration of 2 m/s² for 4 seconds. Find the displacement (in m) of this body in these 4 seconds.
questions.solution:
To solve this problem we will use the following equation,

s = ut + (1)/(2)a{t²}

Substitute u = 5, a = 2 and t = 4

s = 5 × 4 + (1)/(2) × 2 × 4²

s = 36 m

Hence, displacement is 36 m.

questions.question: If the velocity of a body is halved its kinetic energy ________.
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__**:** 

__
 
• **Velocity**: The **rate of change of displacement** is called **velocity**.

 
 
• It is denoted by V and **SI unit** is **m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic energy**: The **energy of a particle** **due to its motion** is called **kinetic energy**.
 
 
• It is denoted by KE, and the **SI unit **is the **joule (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic energy** is given by:

K.E = (1)/(2)m{v²}

Where m is the mass of the body.

**CALCULATION**__:

 
• Kinetic energy is given by:

Rightarrow K.E = (1)/(2)m{v²}

 
• So, if we substitute (1)/(2)v instead of v, then we will obtain

Rightarrow K.E₁=(1)/(2)mtimes({(1)/(2)v)²}=(1)/(2)mtimes(1)/(4){v²} = (1)/(4)( {K.E} )

 
• Hence** the kinetic energy becomes a quarter of the original**. So option 2 is correct.

questions.question: Plants utilise ________ from the atmosphere for photosynthesis.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Carbon dioxide.__**

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• Plants use the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere to synthesize sugar which acts as their food source.
 
• This process can only take place in the presence of sunlight which is why the process is known as ‘photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis is the process through which green plants synthesize or prepare carbohydrates or food from sunlight, carbon dioxide (CO2), and water.__
 
• Photosynthesis is a reduction process that involves the reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates.
 
• In the presence of light, green plants fix carbon dioxide to complex molecules like carbohydrates.
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplast of the cell.
 
• Chlorophyll is a green pigment that is found in the leaves of plants. 
 
• It helps plants to absorb sunlight energy. 
 
• This energy is used to prepare food by combining carbon dioxide and water.
 
• Plants with chlorophyll pigments may perform photosynthesis by absorbing light energy. 
 
• The conversion of light energy to chemical energy occurs during the photosynthesis process.
 
• The splitting of water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen is known as photooxidation.

questions.question: In Microsoft Excel, left arrow key stroke leads to ______ movement on a spreadsheet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** One cell Left.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• MS-Excel:-

 
 
• It is a **spreadsheet program for data analysis and documentation.**
 
• It contains a **number of rows and columns, where the intersection of a column and cell and a row is a "cell".**
 
• **Each cell contains one point of data.**
 
• It is developed by **Microsoft**.
 
• It** features calculation, graphing tools, pivot tables.**
 
• **Pressing the left arrow** keystroke leads to the selection of a cell which is one cell to the left of the previously selected cell.
 
• The** arrow keys can be further used to navigate through cells using up, down, left and right directions.**
